description: The bar chart illustrates the effect sizes of various multilingual BERT models across different language families and isolated language groups, with error bars indicating variability. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by language family, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," quantifies the magnitude of the effect, ranging from 0 to 30. Each language family or group is represented by a cluster of bars, with each bar corresponding to a specific model variant: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The legend clarifies the color coding for each model. The chart shows that the effect sizes vary significantly across language families and models. For instance, in the IE-Indic family, the mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ models exhibit the highest effect sizes, both exceeding 20, while in the IE-Baltic family, the effects are generally lower, with most models showing values below 10. The Isolate and Uralic categories show very low effect sizes for all models, with values close to zero. The Semitic family shows a notable increase in effect for the XLM-B₂ model, which reaches approximately 20, while the mBERT-L₂ model shows a negative effect, around -5. The error bars suggest that the variability in effect sizes is generally higher for models with larger effect sizes.
